newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Cbank dlr sales halts Mauritius rupee slide in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Cbank dlr sales halts Mauritius rupee slide in Oct.

text.p: A weakening trend in the Mauritius rupee versus the dollar was halted in October by central bank dollar sales in the interbank foreign exchange market, the central Bank of Mauritius (BoM) said on Tuesday.

"The salient feature of the interbank foreign exchange market in October was the arrest of accelerated depreciation of the Rupee vis-a-vis the dollar. The market continued to be dominated by BoM sales of the dollar to commercial banks," the central bank said in a report.

"...the weighted average intervention rate in October was 20.5795 rupees per dollar while the weighted average transaction rate in the interbank forex market was 20.5861 rupees per dollar," the central banks said.

The central bank said it sold a total $46.6 million in market interventions in October and made no purchases. In September, a total $23.85 million was sold during market interventions while purchases again, amounted to zero.
The central bank said the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate sold a total $13.17 million to commercial banks in October, up from $12.39 million in September.

From August, the Syndicate sells directly to banks 25 percent of the island's hard currency receipts obtained from sugar exports. The remaining 75 percent is kept by the Bank of Mauritius for market interventions.

The central bank said commercial banks' forex shortfalls, net payments over receipts, totalled $37.20 million in October from $34.44 million in September. It said the shortfalls were covered by market interventions.

Foreign exchange reserves in the central bank stood at 14.893 billion rupees at October-end, representing 20.5 weeks of the island's imports needs based on revised 1995/96 import bills. Central banks forex reserves totalled 15.068 billion rupees on September 1996, representing 21.8 weeks of imports.
In money market (treasury bills auctions) operations, the average bank rate eased 4.0 basis points to 9.65 percent in October from 9.69 percent in September, the report said.
The report said the central bank auctioned 3.000 billion rupees of treasury bills in October, received bids worth 2.530 billion rupees and accepted 2.365 billion rupees of the bids.
In September, the central bank put 2.675 billion rupees of treasury bills on tender, received 2.698 billion rupees of bids and accepted 2.047 billion rupees of the bids.

"The average weighted yield on 91-day bills increased from 9.32 percent in September 1996 to 9.48 percent in October 1996. However, the average weighted yields on 182-day, 364-day bills remained unchanged at 9.34 percent and 9.50 percent, respectively," the report said.
"Market preferences switched from 364-day bills in September 1996 to 182-day bills in October 1996," it added.

The central bank report said narrow money M1 (currency in public plus demand deposits in banking system) rose by 4.8 percent in September to 8.711 billion rupees from 8.309 billion rupees in August. Broad money M2 (M1 plus savings deposits and time deposits) gained 1.0 percent to 54.328 billion rupees in September from 53.781 billion rupees in August.
